data.name: Exact-description novelty
data.research_question: Can exact novelty in verbalised event descriptions separate attack events without learning a statistical model?
data.hypothesis: A purely novelty-based rule will over-alert because most attack-test descriptions are also present in benign training data.
data.representation: V2 full-provenance event description (operations, entities and directed relationships)
data.training_strategy: Memorise the set of 13,029 unique training descriptions.
data.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.897235 and Average Precision 0.003367. All 70 original positives were flagged, but 20,722 false positives produced precision of 0.337%.
data.interpretation: Description novelty alone captures some attack signal, but 79.39% of attack-test descriptions were seen in training, so novelty is a weak discriminator.
data.limitations: Binary scoring creates large tied blocks; the rule has no notion of semantic similarity.
